vars.task: Use workflow-orchestrator and its bundled DESIGN.md template to write an English draft at plans/preferences-v2/design.md, then identify the one decision needed before execution planning. This is a writable session; I authorize that draft only, and the design is not yet approved. Known facts: a desktop app stores preferences in a local JSON file. V1 readers require a flat object with theme and fontSize, reject a versioned envelope, and V1 writers replace the whole file. V2 needs named profiles and proposes an envelope with schemaVersion, activeProfile and profiles. PreferencesStore owns disk reads and writes; the UI uses its load/save interface. We have agreed that the new loader recognizes both shapes, maps V1 values to a default profile in memory, and validates before exposing state to the UI. Saves use a temporary sibling file and atomic replacement on the same filesystem; the in-memory saved state advances only after replacement succeeds. Validation or disk failures must reach the caller and preserve the last valid saved file; corrupt input must not be silently replaced by defaults. The existing single-process writer assumption remains; cloud sync and concurrent writers are out of scope. Success means V2 reads an existing V1 file without losing its values, round-trips named profiles, and reports a failed save without claiming persistence. The sole unresolved decision is whether users must still be able to open and edit preferences using V1 after their first V2 save. Product has not answered, and the current envelope proposal breaks V1 reads. Capture the known responsibilities, read/save flow, failure behavior, compatibility trade-off and migration direction. You may recommend an option, but do not decide backward write compatibility for us or invent an approved migration. Do not implement, write an execution plan or ask unrelated questions.
